/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 18 August 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2815 (-63)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4452 (-138)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2155 (-51)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1631 (3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 866 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market came under further pressure today, with the Pacific leading the decline while the Atlantic remained steady but lacked activity. The BCI 182 5TC fell $1,250 to $40,375. The C5 index dropped $0.750 to $13.485, while C3 also eased, down $0.130 to $35.850. In the Pacific, sentiment remained soft. Much of yesterday’s C5 fixing was concluded post-index and later in the day, making for a fairly busy start, with most fixtures done at a tick below $14. Offers today opened in the low $14s before easing towards $14 during the afternoon. Bids started around $13.00, with two miners reportedly fixing at $13.40. Three C5 miners were in the market today. The Atlantic remained steady but quiet. A couple of Fronthaul fixtures in the North Atlantic provided some support, although overall activity was limited. South Brazil and West Africa to China remained subdued, with little in the way of a meaningful bid and offers reported around $36 to the low $36s.
PANAMAX
It was a weaker day across both the Atlantic and Pacific basins, with the P5TC declining by $462 to close at $19,391 as negative sentiment continued to weigh on the market. In the Atlantic, brokers reported a substantial tonnage count, with both ballasters from the Far East and prompt tonnage within the basin contributing to oversupply. Market participants noted a limited volume of fresh trans-Atlantic mineral cargo demand, forcing owners to lower their rate expectations. The few fixtures concluded were reported below previous market levels, further reinforcing the softer sentiment. Fundamentals for both the fronthaul and trans-Atlantic routes remain under pressure, with vessel supply continuing to outpace cargo demand. The Pacific market is showing a similar trend, with reported fixture volumes remaining subdued. Market sources indicate that owners are reluctant to significantly lower their rate expectations, supported by relatively steady demand from both Australia and the North Pacific. However, some participants noted that a number of earlier-positioned vessels have accepted discounted rates in order to secure employment, highlighting the underlying pressure on the market despite pockets of activity.
SUPRAMAX
Similar to yesterday, there was minimal movement on all routes in today’s Index, with another small increase in the 11TC average up $42 to $20,614. The Mediterranean continues to struggle with an oversupply of tonnage, the Continent seems to be easing due to the lack of scrap and the US Gulf appeared fairly static. The South has showed some positive signs but seems positional and the Indian Ocean might have slowed its descent, from South Africa at least. In Asia sentiment is positive without much uplift in rates so far this week. ADM reportedly took an Ultramax delivery US Gulf end August for a trip East Mediterranean with grains at $32,000, but there were no further details. The Sun Vil II (56,042 2013) prompt in Rizhao fixed a trip to West Africa intention bagged cement at $14,000 for the 1st 65 days, but the split rate and the Charterer remained elusive, and the Zhe Hai 525 (57,283 2011) Shanwei 21st August was said to have fixed via Indonesia back to South China with nickel ore at around $17,000-18,000 to an unnamed Charterer.
HANDYSIZE
Building on the previous day’s tone, the Handysize market saw another relatively subdued session, with limited activity reported across most regions. The BHSI increased by 2 points to 866, while the 7TC average rose by $32 to settle at $15,585. In the Continent and Mediterranean, market conditions remained soft, with little visible activity and limited fresh enquiry keeping rates under pressure. Across the South Atlantic and US Gulf, changes were minimal and the market appeared broadly balanced, with rates recorded a tick higher than last done as fundamentals showed little sign of any notable shift. In Asia however, the market remained better supported, underpinned by tight prompt tonnage and a steady flow of cargoes. This helped sustain a more constructive tone across several loading areas, although fixing information remained relatively limited. On fixtures, the Pas Blue Wave (31,889 2010) open Colombo 18–21 August was fixed to Vietnam with steels at $8,750, while the Asahi Bulker (33,179 2012) open Singapore was fixed delivery September for two to three laden legs by Mayborne Bulk, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
CISA Daily Crude Steel Production

In the period 1-10 August, daily crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills climbed 5.8% from the preceding eleven days to 2.0 Mt/day, industry association data show. However, output stood 4.9% below the same period last year.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
The front continued to tilt lower in the morning session off the back of weaker physical sentiment, with the index sliding down 1,250 on the day, to 36,872, all while deferred contracts remained relatively firm. A few additional buyers stepped in towards close, with Sep bid up to 39200 after trading down to lows of 38750. Aug was active, trading 38750 down to 38450, closing at 38600. Oct traded 40400 down to lows of 40000, closing at the highs for the day. Q4 closed flat on the day, after trading 38900-38500. Cal27 printed once at 30750. Cal28 printed 26800 and 26900.

PMX
The pmx curve moved lower through the session today. August traded between 19,750–19,850, with activity relatively light despite a few larger clips. September was again the main focus, trading between 20,100–20,750. Early activity was concentrated around 20,400–20,500, before the market softened steadily through the day to around 20,100–20,150 into the close. October traded between 21,150–21,550, with the strongest levels seen during the morning before easing later in the session. Q4 26 traded between 19,850–20,800, finishing towards the lower end of that range. Q1 27 was sold down to 16,600, with repeated clips at 16,750 early on. Further out, Cal 27 traded between 17,300–17,400.

selected_cards.content: ATLANTIC: Off the back of a firmer end to last week in the Handysize Continent market, it has been a rather sluggish start this week with little fresh enquiry and no fixtures to report, which could result in downward pressure on rates.
